title: Maps and Key-Value Data
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of maps and key-value data and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—the map interface—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study maps and key-value data with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you select data structures according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update needs. In this lesson, focus on the map interface and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

items.title: The Map interface
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

items.title: Keys and values
items.text: Choose a collection by its contract: ordering, uniqueness, key lookup, insertion/removal cost, and iterator behavior. Do not assume every implementation preserves order or supports concurrent mutation. Apply that reasoning specifically to keys and values and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

items.title: Mapping and lookup
items.text: Choose a collection according to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and update requirements. Review equals/hashCode contracts, iteration behavior, and concurrent-modification rules before selecting an implementation.
